newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends slightly up, light buying by RBI.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends slightly up, light buying by RBI.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended dull on Tuesday at 35.790/795 per dollar after being stuck in a narrow range through the day, dealers said.
"Most of the day's trade was around 35.795," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There was hardly any movement in the exchange rate today."
He said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) made small dollar purchases at 35.795.
"But the amounts were very small," he said. "I doubt whether RBI would have bought more than $10 million today. Their purchases had no impact at all on the exchange rate."
Dealers were bullish about the prospects of the rupee and said the rupee was likely to move up unless the central bank bought dollars aggressively.
"Given the present supply in the market, only major RBI dollar purchases can keep the rupee down," said another dealer. "There is virtually no demand other than from RBI at the moment."
Dealers said forward premiums were steady after opening slightly down.
"Forward premiums opened marginally down as call money has eased and is expected to remain easy in the coming days," said a dealer.
Call money ended Tuesday at 5.0-5.5 percent against Monday's close of 6.25-6.5 percent. Call money was traded in a 7.0-8.0 percent range most of last week.
"But there was little movement in forward premiums from opening levels," the dealer said.
November-delivery dollars ended Tuesday at a premium of 85/87 paise against Monday's close of 86/88.
